Dear Professor Hemmings,

We thank you for considering our **Research Communication** manuscript titled *"The inherent bias in studies reporting outcomes using total opioid burden metrics: a simulation study"* to the British Journal of Anaesthesia. 


Our paper is a methodological critique of total opioid burden metrics such as oral morphine equivalent (OME) that finds an important measurement bias.
The bias is present in any study comparing groups with unmatched proportions of differing opioid or there is an error in the conversion values used compared to the biological ground truth. Whilst this applies predominantly to observational research, there are key implications for randomised controlled trials. 

Despite multiple attempts to unify the methodology with conversion tables and calculator tools, the inherent bias continues to be overlooked. With over 4,000 papers in the literature using or describing TOB metrics in the past 10 years, the impact of the this work will be significant ^[From PUBMED search of *"(Milligram morphine equivalent) OR (Oral morphine equivalent)"* filtered to the last 10 years on 16th September 2026]. We hope this paper will lead to a critical review of how total opioid burden metrics are used in research and improve the accuracy in the metrics already widely used. 

We can confirm no parts of this work have been presented before and has not been under consideration at any other journal. 

Many thanks,
The authors
